precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; the Lord is a God of knowledge and by him actions are weighed. He raiseth up the poor out of the dust and lifteth the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes and make them inherit the throne of glory.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 5:11 says the Lord will “set up on high those that be low.” That is us: we are low right now, but he is going to set us up on high. And “those which mourn may be exalted to safety”: our people that mourn shall be exalted to safety and comfort. 1 Samuel 2 goes with it.

“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth.” The arrogancy is the foolishness, the teaching and the wisdom of this world. Pastor, don’t let that come out of your mouth. “For the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” He is going to judge all of us on our actions. Not your thoughts, though you must control your thoughts, but on what you do.

“The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.” “The Lord killeth, and maketh alive”: it is the Lord that kills and the Lord that makes alive. “The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.” That is what Job 5:11 just said: we are being brought low, but we are going to be exalted.

“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust.” The dust represents confusion, a low state of confusion, and the poor are the poor in spirit. “And lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill.” We are the beggar. Our people are begging for reparations, give us money; I want Section 8, I want a job, I want this. And the dunghill is this low place: whatever kind of house you have, compared to where we came from, it is a dunghill.

But he lifts them up “to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.” The Lord is going to make us inherit the throne of glory. That is the setting up on high of those that be low in Job 5:11.

precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth, for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. He wants action, not lip service.
precepts.point: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge, that I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth? The Bible is God's excellent things, not a prosperity tool or a debate about what we feel like doing. He expects excellence, so change your mind to his standard instead of the crumbs society leaves our people.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.”

Actions are weighed when it comes to the Most High. That is why he gave us the excellent things of Proverbs 22:20: to learn them and apply them, because he wants actions behind those things. Not lip service, but actual action from all of us that he called.

Romans 15:4 says the scriptures were written for our learning; 1 Samuel 2:3 says what he does with that learning. He weighs what we do with it. Proud talk and arrogancy out of the mouth weigh nothing with him, because he is a God of knowledge and knows whether the words are backed by works.

That is the pride of thine heart: to talk big about the things of God and not live them. The one who has been given the excellent things has to put his actions where his mouth is, and keep arrogancy out of it.

precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly, let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed; saying God knows my heart while breaking his laws is speaking proudly.
precepts.point: Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands; brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama. When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him; your actions show you actually hate him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” What the Lord requires of Israel is not talk. It is to fear him, walk in all his ways, love him, serve him with all thy heart and with all thy soul, and “keep the commandments of the Lord, and his statutes, which I command thee this day for thy good”. He is a God of knowledge, and he weighs actions, not words.

Saying God knows my heart while breaking his laws is speaking proudly; that is arrogancy coming out of the mouth. Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands. Brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama.

When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him. Your actions show you actually hate him, and by him actions are weighed.

precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes”: do is the action word. The Most High is a God of doing. “Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” He does not weigh your talk; he weighs your actions.

So do not talk proudly and arrogantly, saying God loves me no matter what, God knows my heart. The Most High had a personal relationship with a few men, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel and David. Talking like you are one of them is arrogancy coming out of your mouth. What he weighs is whether you observe to do his commandments.

precepts.text: The Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
precepts.point: All the silver and gold and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the Lord, separated and sanctified for his treasury alone: nobody was to gain personally from this war.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

precepts.why:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” Words say a lot, but actions always speak louder, and by him actions are weighed.

Rahab's actions were weighed and she lived. And the warning cuts the other way: keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it. Your individual sins affect the whole nation of Israel, your brothers, your sisters, and the children. That is why we must examine ourselves whether we be in the faith. The silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the Lord, separated and sanctified for his treasury alone: nobody was to gain personally from this war.

precepts.text: Why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say? You cannot just say you love the Lord, that you believe in the God of Israel, and do nothing of what he says: not loving your neighbour, holding grudges and envy, respecting leadership above your own husband who is Christ in the house.
precepts.point: All of us in this walk, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, have taken covenant and proclaimed out of our mouths that we are going to endure to the end; we broke the bread and drank the wine and took the covenant with the Lord. Now the Lord is judging you by your actions: are you going to endure to the end, whether to Christ's return or until you leave this earth, if you truly love him?

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” “the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” What the Lord weighs is actions: if it came out of your mouth, are you going to do it?

You cannot just say you love the Lord, that you believe in the God of Israel, and do nothing of what he says: not loving your neighbour, holding grudges and envy, respecting leadership above your own husband who is Christ in the house.

Saying, I have a personal relationship with God, God knows my heart, God loves me no matter what: that is arrogancy coming out of the mouth. The scripture says he loves you if you keep the commandments. Hannah said, “let not arrogancy come out of your mouth.”

precepts.text: The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first, that the inhabitants of Jerusalem, which were Benjamin and Levi in there with Judah, do not magnify themselves against Judah. That is why you see so many of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi in the truth right now, with the northern kingdom trickling in; the Most High gives the head tribes what is most important first, not worldly things but the truth of who they are, to raise up the twelve tribes of Jacob. And he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David, and the house of David shall be as God: all twelve tribes, as the angel of the Lord before them.
precepts.point: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
The Lord is prophesying through Hannah: “The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.” Zechariah shows who that is.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The inhabitants of Jerusalem were Benjamin and Levi, in there with Judah. That is why you see so many of Judah, Benjamin and Levi in the truth right now, with the northern kingdom trickling in. The Most High gives the head tribes what is most important first: not worldly things, but the truth of who they are, to raise up the twelve tribes of Jacob.

Then: “and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David; and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.” That is all twelve tribes. He that is feeble shall be as David goes right back to “they that stumbled are girded with strength”: that is the house of Israel.

precepts.text: David said, by my God have I leaped over a wall; David was a mighty man of war.
precepts.point: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
David said, “For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall.” David was a mighty man of war.

So when Zechariah says “he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”, that is the strength in view: “they that stumbled are girded with strength.”

precepts.text: His feet like hinds' feet, fast like a deer, and a bow of steel broken by his arms: David bent steel, took down lions and bears, and killed a giant with a rock and a sling. He that is feeble shall be as David goes right back to they that stumbled are girded with strength; that is the house of Israel.
precepts.point: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“He maketh my feet like hinds’ feet, and setteth me upon my high places. He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.” His feet were fast like a deer, and a bow of steel was broken by his arms. David bent steel, took down lions and bears, and killed a giant with a rock and a sling.

Zechariah's word, “he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”, goes right back to Hannah's word, “they that stumbled are girded with strength.” That is the house of Israel.

In the same verses Hannah is talking about herself: “the barren hath born seven; and she that hath many children is waxed feeble.”

precepts.text: See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand. There is no Buddha, there is no Allah, there is no Krishna; all of that is made-up imaginations of men.
precepts.point: The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord decides who wakes up and the Lord decides who passes; that is all of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.”

That is Hannah's word: “The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.” The Lord decides who wakes up and the Lord decides who passes; that is all of the Lord.

He says, “there is no god with me.” There is no Buddha, there is no Allah, there is no Krishna; all of that is made-up imaginations of men.

precepts.text: For your newer brothers and sisters, Ecclesiasticus is the book also called Sirach: prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, all come of the Lord.
precepts.point: The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.” Ecclesiasticus, the book also called Sirach, says the same: “Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of the Lord.”

All of it comes of the Lord, the poverty and the riches, the bringing low and the lifting up.

precepts.text: How is that possible? It is the Lord: he brings low, and he lifts up one that was never thought of. Like David: when Samuel looked at the older brother he thought, he has to be the one, he looks like a king; but the Lord chose the one sitting down upon the ground whom nobody thought of to be the king.
precepts.point: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust: out of the dust means out of confusion; he brings the poor out of confusion, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and he hath set the world upon them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust.” Out of the dust means out of confusion: he brings the poor out of confusion, “and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory.”

“Many kings have sat down upon the ground; and one that was never thought of hath worn the crown.” How is that possible? It is the Lord: he brings low, and he lifts up one that was never thought of.

Like David. When Samuel looked at the older brother he thought, he has to be the one, he looks like a king. But the Lord chose the one sitting down upon the ground, whom nobody thought of, to be the king. All of it is his, “for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.”

precepts.text: As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
precepts.point: Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way; but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
Joshua said, “choose you this day whom ye will serve”, and then: “but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.”

Eli did not hold his house to that. The man of God asked him, “Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh’s house?” That is talking about Levi, going into Moses. The Lord chose him “out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me”, and gave his father's house “all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel.” They had need of nothing; they were well taken care of.

“Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me”? You are disrespecting me, is what he is saying: I am supposed to be honoured in everything before the children of Israel, and you let your sons disrespect my offerings.

Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way, but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that. As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.

precepts.text: I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment. The Most High said, I know how Abraham gets down; he is not going to let his kids be out of order.
precepts.point: That is why the Lord dealt with Abraham the way he did: Abraham was not going to choose his kids above the Most High, and they were going to do all that he commanded.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
The Lord told Eli, “them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.” Lightly esteemed means the Lord is not really looking out for you: you are not thinking about me, so I am not thinking about you; go ahead and see how it works out for yourself.

That is why the Lord dealt with Abraham the way he did. “For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.” The Most High said, I know how Abraham gets down; he is not going to let his kids be out of order. Abraham was not going to choose his kids above the Most High, and they were going to do all that he commanded.

Eli did the opposite. He honoured his sons above the Lord, and so the Lord said of his house, “Be it far from me.”

precepts.text: Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws. This is what was going on in the tent of Abraham as long as he lived: all the laws that applied to Abraham at that time, he kept them, the sabbath day included; other laws would apply after Israel came out of Egypt.
precepts.point: That is why the Lord dealt with Abraham the way he did: Abraham was not going to choose his kids above the Most High, and they were going to do all that he commanded.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” This is what was going on in the tent of Abraham as long as he lived. All the laws that applied to Abraham at that time, he kept them, the sabbath day included; other laws would apply after Israel came out of Egypt.

That is honouring the Lord, and “them that honour me I will honour.”

precepts.text: If he beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, that lifts up his eyes to the idols and commits abomination, he shall not live: he hath done all these abominations; he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him. The son that continues in the sins of his father dies for his own doings.
precepts.point: Why would the Lord judge the children of future generations of Eli's house? The thought might be, he is killing them for the sins of their forefather; I thought the sons did not die for the fathers. Ezekiel 18 shows what it is talking about: the judgment falls on the son that continues in the sins of his father.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father’s house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house.” Cutting off the arm means cutting off thy strength, and it was talking about his children. The Lord was going to kill Eli's descendants young: “all the increase of thine house shall die in the flower of their age”, in the full strength and peak of their youth.

Why would the Lord judge the children of future generations of Eli's house? The thought might be, he is killing them for the sins of their forefather; I thought the sons did not die for the fathers. Ezekiel 18 shows what it is talking about: “If he beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood”, that “hath lifted up his eyes to the idols, hath committed abomination”: “shall he then live? he shall not live: he hath done all these abominations; he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him.”

The judgment falls on the son that continues in the sins of his father, and he dies for his own doings. Eli's descendants were going to follow in the same way of their fathers, the sons of Belial, doing wickedness and evil. Because Eli did not reprove his sons, the generations after would follow right in their footsteps.

precepts.text: But if he beget a son that seeth all his father's sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like, he shall not die for the iniquity of his father; he shall surely live. Eating upon the mountains is partaking in the heathen's idol worship, the food and the drink that went into it, as when Israel rose up to eat and to play before the calf.
precepts.point: Why would the Lord judge the children of future generations of Eli's house? The thought might be, he is killing them for the sins of their forefather; I thought the sons did not die for the fathers. Ezekiel 18 shows what it is talking about: the judgment falls on the son that continues in the sins of his father.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father’s sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like”, “he shall not die for the iniquity of his father, he shall surely live.”

Eating upon the mountains is partaking in the heathen's idol worship, the food and the drink that went into it, as when Israel rose up to eat and to play before the calf. The son who “hath not eaten upon the mountains, neither hath lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel”, who “hath executed my judgments, hath walked in my statutes”, lives.

So the cutting off of Eli's house was not the sons dying for the father. The Lord cut them off in the strength of their youth because they were going to follow in the same way of their fathers.

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding.
precepts.point: That is the same man we have to be: faithful unto the Lord, doing all that is in his heart and in his mind, not in our own. We cannot lean upon our own understanding, and we cannot lean upon our own emotions and how we feel; in whatever situation, at any given moment, it is what did the Lord say. Do not let the old man guide you and lead you; it should be the spirit of Christ which is in you, the hidden man.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.”

The sign to Eli was that his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, “in one day they shall die both of them.” And the Lord said, “I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.”

That is the same man we have to be: faithful unto the Lord, doing all that is in his heart and in his mind, not in our own. We cannot lean upon our own understanding, and we cannot lean upon our own emotions and how we feel. In whatever situation, at any given moment, it is what did the Lord say. Do not let the old man guide you and lead you; it should be the spirit of Christ which is in you, the hidden man.

precepts.text: The Most High is a God of knowledge, and by Him actions are weighed.
precepts.point: The covenant is to such as keep His commandments and remember them to do them. To do them is an action word.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
The mercy of the Lord is “To such as keep his covenant, and to those that remember his commandments to do them.” To do them is an action word.

Hannah says what the Most High weighs: “Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” The Most High is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. Not talk, actions.

So remembering the commandments is not enough; the mercy is to those that remember them to do them, and the doing is what he weighs.

precepts.text: The Most High maketh poor and maketh rich, he bringeth low and lifteth up.
precepts.point: We already understood that the Most High can bring one up and set another down, but the heathen had to learn it by being jacked up, literally turned to crawl like a bird with the heart of a beast; as soon as his understanding returned he praised the one true living God.

note.label: Daniel 4: Nebuchadnezzar Abased Until He Knew the Most High Rules

precepts.why:
“The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.” That is what happened to Nebuchadnezzar. The Most High brought him low, jacked him up, literally turned him to crawl like a bird with the heart of a beast; then he lifted him up again. His reason returned, and “for the glory of my kingdom, mine honour and brightness returned unto me”; his counsellors and his lords sought unto him, and excellent majesty was added unto him.

We already understood that the Most High can bring one up and set another down. But the heathen had to learn it by being jacked up. As soon as his understanding returned he praised the one true living God: “Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.” Rich or poor, high or low, it is in the hand of the Lord, and pride is what he abases.

precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly, for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
precepts.point: Talk is not what is weighed. Israel is judged by our doings.

note.label: Zechariah 1: Turn Ye Unto Me, and I Will Turn Unto You

precepts.why:
Our fathers returned and said, according to our ways and according to our doings, so hath he dealt with us. You get judged by the Most High based on your actions. “Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.”

Talk is not what is weighed. The Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed; Israel is judged by our doings.

precepts.text: The Most High maketh poor and maketh rich, he bringeth low and lifteth up, raising the poor out of the dust and the beggar from the dunghill.
precepts.point: The Most High is the one who brings a man low. Sometimes he withholds money, status, or a job to hinder a man from sinning, the way he removed King Manasseh from his power. Many hurtful lusts come from the love of money, and celebrities get caught up in wickedness because riches in the hand of a man who has sin become a tool for evil. He wants to teach you discipline and contentment first, so that when the money comes it is only a tool to pay your bills and support the truth, not to live in the delicacies of this life.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.” The Most High is the one who brings a man low. A lot of times we do not know why he put a person in that condition, which is why, when people at camp ask if we give money to the poor, we say no. The money could end up feeding a drug dealer, a drug addict or a child molester without our knowing it.

Peter had no silver and gold to give the man, and what he gave him was better. It is the Most High who “raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes”, in his own time and his own way.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

precepts.why: “Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth”. “for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” It ain't about what your mouth says or your good deeds. He don't give a damn about that. Your actions prove who you are, what type of man you are. If you can't be about your word, you won't be taken seriously. God gives you your reward from your actions.

points: Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation. This is what we read about last week, where Eli's children would take the sacrifice from the people before it was ready.

And honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people. That is the error that some fathers and mothers make. You honour your children above the Lord, and now you end up in jail, beat up, or dead.

When you read the chapter, God told Eli the high priest to correct his kids. He corrected them about sleeping with the women around the temple, but he never corrected them about stealing the sacrificed meat — because he benefited from it.

How does that deal with us today? Easy. Many times you will have a young man or young woman selling drugs, and that young man will give the mother thousands of dollars a week, and she is very happy and quiet. And we have had several cases: as soon as the young man repents and says I am going to change my life, guess who is mad? Mama. You are in a cult. Look what they did to you, they destroyed my baby. But when he was selling drugs, killing half the community, he was her angel. She loved that boy above God.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Still going with bad kids. Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord.
See that? The high priest's sons were children of Belial, meaning wicked kids. They were wicked sons.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: Now Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel. See, he heard what his sons did unto all Israel. Good.
And how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. So Hophni and Phinehas was sexing the women that were preparing to have sacrifices done. Right?

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: And he said unto them, Why do ye such things? For I hear of your evil dealings by all this people. Nay, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear: ye make the Lord's people to transgress.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: Also before they burnt the fat, the priest's servant came, and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: And if any man said unto him, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently — let me finish roasting and let me finish cooking it, good — and then take as much as thy soul desireth. Then when it is finished, you all could take as much as you desire.
Then he would answer him, Nay. And this is what their servant would say to them. But thou shalt give it me now.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up. Who did you think made us poor?

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

points: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill. This is Hannah's prayer; the Holy Spirit through a woman said this. Why beggars? Because we are the ones always begging another race of people for reparations, for jobs, for services, instead of building with our own, because our own are not well as a people. And the dunghill is not just one poor country; wherever we live in this captivity has been made a dunghill compared to what we came from, because we came from ruling.

To set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and he hath set the world upon them. From the dunghill to the throne of glory: that is planet rulership.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

points: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.

Your actions will be weighed. We are going to be judged off our actions, our works, period. You have to prove yourself to the Lord: that you are studying, the works you do in this body, constantly growing, constantly consistent.

We are the representation of this truth. When they look at the Israelites as a face, who do they look toward? The brothers in the purple and gold, Israel United in Christ. Why? Because our leadership is heavy on integrity, character, structure, and order: traits we were never taught growing up and have to be taught now, around men who have built themselves up.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

points: Talk no more so exceeding proudly, I am covered by the blood, I am a Christian; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. Your actions are examined by the Lord. If you are not filling yourself with the commandments of God and studying to show yourself approved, then your actions follow who you really worship, and debauchery and all manner of wickedness follow that. If you truly follow the God of this Bible, your actions will follow. Your actions are weighed every day; when you wake up you have a choice, continue on the path of righteousness or fall back, and judgment is waiting. Brothers who go into the highways and byways teaching our people to repent: do not stop; our people are depending on you. Satan is always on his A game; we have to stay on ours.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord: I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the Lord: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. What the Lord weighs is actions: if it came out of your mouth, are you going to do it?

All of us in this walk, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, have taken covenant and proclaimed out of our mouths that we are going to endure to the end; we broke the bread and drank the wine and took the covenant with the Lord. Now the Lord is judging you by your actions: are you going to endure to the end, whether to Christ's return or until you leave this earth, if you truly love him?
"I have a personal relationship with God; God knows my heart; God loves me no matter what": that is arrogancy coming out of the mouth. The scripture says he loves you if you keep the commandments.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: They that were full have hired out themselves for bread: so that the barren hath born seven, and she that hath many children is waxed feeble. Hannah is talking about herself there.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord decides who wakes up and the Lord decides who passes; that is all of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust: out of the dust means out of confusion; he brings the poor out of confusion, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and he hath set the world upon them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail. The adversaries of the Lord shall be broken to pieces; and he shall give strength unto his king, which is Christ, and exalt the horn of his anointed.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Elkanah went to Ramah to his house, and the child did minister unto the Lord before Eli the priest. Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord. They were the devil.

They were Levites, priests in the house of the Lord doing the work of the Lord, and yet it says they knew not the Lord. Why? Because they did not keep the commandments true in their spirit; they kept it on the surface where you can see it. They looked the part: they had on the fringes, they had the beard, they showed up on the sabbath day; but their spirit was not right with the Lord, and they were really the sons of the devil. Do not let that be you, Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: The priests' custom with the people was that when any man offered sacrifice, the priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand, and struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. They would dip it in, and what came up was the priest's portion of meat for that day; all the Levites did that, based on the sacrifices Israel brought in.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: This is how the Lord took care of Levi. He told Levi in the law that Levi would have no inheritance of land among the tribes; the Lord provided for them through the sacrifices that Israel brought, so they had need of nothing.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Also, before they burnt the fat, the priest's servant came and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw: I will cook it up my own way, give it to me now, before it is done. And if any man said, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth, he would answer, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: These were devils serving in the house of the Lord, strong-arming the offerings. Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord: for men abhorred the offering of the Lord. These priests were disrespecting the offering of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: But Samuel ministered before the Lord, being a child, girded with a linen ephod; moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, The Lord give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the Lord. And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived and bare three sons and two daughters; and the child Samuel grew before the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel, and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: the harlots hanging around the temple, and Eli's sons dealing with them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: He said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people; ye make the Lord's people to transgress. The Levites were the leaders, so the people followed their actions: what the priests did, the people did also. They saw the sons of Eli sleeping with the harlots and said, it must be all right, look what they have, look how they live in the temple; let us follow their lead.

Eli might have said something to his children, but he did not remove them and put them out of the priesthood for their evil dealings; he said something, but he did not go further than words, he took no action with it. Watch what happened to his children.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the Lord would slay them. And the child Samuel grew on, and was in favour both with the Lord, and also with men.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way; but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: There came a man of God unto Eli, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh's house? That is talking about Levi, going into Moses. Did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel? They had need of nothing; they were well taken care of.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me? You are disrespecting me, is what he is saying: I am supposed to be honoured in everything before the children of Israel, and you let your sons disrespect my offerings.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Wherefore the Lord God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the Lord saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed. Lightly esteemed means the Lord is not really looking out for you: you are not thinking about me, so I am not thinking about you; go ahead and see how it works out for yourself.
That is why the Lord dealt with Abraham the way he did: Abraham was not going to choose his kids above the Most High, and they were going to do all that he commanded.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father's house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house. Cutting off the arm means cutting off thy strength: it was talking about his children. He was going to kill Eli's descendants young, and all the increase of his house would die in the flower of their age, in the full strength and peak of their youth.

Why would the Lord judge the children of future generations of Eli's house? The thought might be, he is killing them for the sins of their forefather; I thought the sons did not die for the fathers. Ezekiel 18 shows what it is talking about: the judgment falls on the son that continues in the sins of his father.

So why would the Lord cut off all those descendants of Eli in the strength of their youth? Because they were going to follow in the same way of their fathers, the sons of Belial, doing wickedness and evil; because Eli did not reprove his sons, the generations after would follow right in their footsteps.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall die both of them. And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind; and I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.

That is the same man we have to be: faithful unto the Lord, doing all that is in his heart and in his mind, not in our own. We cannot lean upon our own understanding, and we cannot lean upon our own emotions and how we feel; in whatever situation, at any given moment, it is what did the Lord say. Do not let the old man guide you and lead you; it should be the spirit of Christ which is in you, the hidden man.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: It shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thine house shall come and crouch to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread. The Lord was going to make it hard on the descendants of Eli: he removed them from the priesthood, and it was written down that the descendants of Eli were not to be allowed into the house of the Lord any more.

Remember, Levi was given no inheritance of land; so how would they eat, how would they live, how would they survive? Receiving their inheritance and their goods was based on them doing what thus saith the Lord told them to do, teaching the laws. Cut off from the priesthood, Eli's house was left to beg.
